The comps: the 30 Dow Jones Industrial names against the peers that share their business

Fetched 2026-10-20 16:31–16:38 UTC, 20 Oct 2026 (midday ET), from FMP through the project's own door. One forward basis (next twelve months, consensus). Peer sets chosen by business, 5–8 names each, reason printed. Medians, premium/discount, implied price per multiple, the analysts' range, today's price, a verdict in three sentences and the thing a peer table cannot see. Banks, brokers and insurers on P/E, PEG and price/book. Loss-makers on EV/sales and EV/gross profit with their cash, debt, burn and runway. Then the ten steadiest earners, the defensive read. The rules and the sources are under PAGE SPECS at the bottom; every figure is in COMPS-DOW30.json beside this page with FMP's raw answers.

The defensive read: the ten with the steadiest earnings

Two measures, both from FMP on the fetch date. NTM-EPS spread = (high − low) ÷ mean of the Street's EPS consensus for the next twelve months (the two fiscal-year rows blended with the same weight as the NTM figures): how far apart the analysts are. FMP carries no estimate-revision history through the proxy, so this dispersion stands in for revision spread; a wide spread is where the next revision comes from. 5-year revenue volatility = standard deviation of the five year-on-year revenue growth rates from the last six fiscal-year income statements, in percentage points. Ranked on the sum of the two ranks; the ten lowest are highlighted. Steady is not cheap: the comps read is printed beside each so the two can be held together.

Verdict

Cheapest name on the page and the only large cheap one: 15.5x NTM earnings against 36.9x for the AI-silicon set (AMD 37x, Marvell 39x, Arm 84x), at parity with Broadcom (17x) and TSMC (20x), and a PEG of 0.20 against 0.43.

The market is paying nothing for the growth because it treats $339B of NTM net income as a peak: a 60% EBIT margin on a $619B revenue consensus that doubles from trailing, with four customers' capex budgets behind it.

The number is FY28 revenue ($695B consensus): a 20% cut leaves the stock at 19x, still under the peer median, so the read only flips if the cycle breaks rather than the estimate.

What comps cannot see here: Comps cannot see customer concentration; every peer in the table is priced on the same four capex budgets.

FMP's own peer list for NVDA: AMD, ARM, AVGO, CBRS, CRWV, INTC, MOVE, MRVL, QCOM, XLAB — 6 of them used here (AMD, ARM, AVGO, INTC, MRVL, QCOM); the rest were left out as a different business or a different cycle, and the set above was chosen from the business line, not the tag.

Verdict

3M is a quarter cheap against the diversified industrials on every row: 16.9x NTM against 22.5x (ITW 22.5x, Emerson 22x, Parker 25x, Eaton 24x, Rockwell 28x; only Dover at 17x is near it), 11.2x EBITDA against 17x.

Half the discount is real and half is arithmetic: trailing net income ($3.5B) carries the PFAS and earplug settlements, so the 48% net-income recovery to $5.2B NTM makes the PEG row (0.35 against 0.60) the highest line on the field, while revenue grows 4.5% against 7.4% for the set.

The number is organic growth: at the peers' 7% the 22.5x re-rate is $228; at 4.5% the market will keep paying a litigation-and-no-growth multiple, and the analysts' $191 says that is what they expect.

What comps cannot see here: A peer table cannot see the remaining PFAS liability, which is a balance-sheet item no multiple here carries.

Verdict

Disney reads cheap only on the PEG row: on the plain multiples it is a shade rich against a cheap set (14.3x NTM against 12.5x; Netflix 18x, Fox 11x, Paramount Skydance 12.5x, Comcast 6x, Sony 17.5x) and 23% over on EV/sales.

The cheap read is a recovery: trailing net income ($8.6B) carries content impairments and the NTM consensus is $13.5B, a 56% jump, so the PEG (0.25 against 0.52) prices the stock at $231 while the earnings row prices it at $98.

The number is FY27 net income: if the $13.5B lands, 12.5x on it is only $98 and the stock is fair, so the read lives on whether the market pays a Netflix multiple (18x, $141) for parks-plus-streaming or a Fox multiple (11x) for it.

What comps cannot see here: Comps cannot see the parks cycle or the sports-rights cost step-up; EBITDA here is a studio number and a parks number added together.

What comps cannot see here: Comps cannot see interchange regulation or stablecoin rails, which are the two things that could put a network on a processor's multiple.

Verdict

The sales row ($50) is the hardware peers' multiple on a company priced as a services annuity, so the midpoint ($95) is an artefact of the set; the honest line is the earnings row: $180 at the peers' 19x, which says the market pays 36x for 13% revenue growth and 8% net-income growth, a PEG of 4.5 against the set's 0.43.

The number is services growth and the gross margin: if services keep compounding at 13%-plus and gross margin holds near 49%, the 36x is a consumer-staples multiple on a platform; at the peers' 19x the stock is $180, and the analysts' $355 is the price.

What comps cannot see here: Comps cannot see the installed base (2.3 billion devices) or the Google search payment, which together are the margin and none of the peers has either.

PEG not priced: NTM net-income growth 8% is outside the 10–100% band where a PEG means anything

What was not done

  • The Dow list is the lane's own: FMP's index-constituent route is not on the proxy's allow-list (checked 20 Oct), so the 30 are the list since the 8 Nov 2024 reconstitution with the one 2026 change found by a web check (Alphabet in for Verizon before the open on 29 Jun 2026; Honeywell kept after spinning off its aerospace arm the same day, per S&P Dow Jones Indices' 23 Jun 2026 announcement). If a later change was missed, one card is wrong, not the method; every symbol was quoted by FMP on the fetch date.
  • Peers were chosen by business line, 5–8 names each, from US listings first and from abroad where the true peer is foreign (Samsung, Xiaomi, Airbus, Komatsu, Siemens, Nestlé, adidas, Puma, AkzoNobel, Nippon Paint, Adyen). No size band was applied; a peer a tenth the size stays in with its reason printed, and the medians carry the count. Several Dow names are the largest and best-margined company in their business, so their peer medians are set by smaller, cheaper names; the card says so where it bends the read (Apple, Visa, Microsoft, McDonald's, Coca-Cola).
  • Multiples are FMP's consensus and statements, not the Hub's stored tables, and not the Hub's tag-based peer sets. FMP's own peer list is printed on each card for the record, with how many of its names were kept.
  • Banks, brokers, insurers and card lenders (Goldman, JPMorgan, Travelers, American Express and their peers) are priced on forward P/E, PEG and price/book only; EV, EV/sales, EV/EBITDA and net debt/EBITDA are not computed for them, and their revenue growth is consensus FY2 over FY1 (a bank's statement revenue is gross of interest expense, consensus is net). This is the one rule added to the CW3 card.
  • The NTM blend is a time-weighted mix of two fiscal-year consensus rows, not a quarter-by-quarter build. For the December fiscal years (most of the 30) that is 20% FY2026 and 80% FY2027 on 20 Oct; for Apple, Visa, Walmart, Nike, Microsoft, Cisco, Disney, Home Depot, Salesforce, Procter and Caterpillar the weight follows their own year-end.
  • Gross margin and net debt/EBITDA are trailing (consensus carries neither). EV/gross profit (loss-makers only; none of the 30 qualifies on 20 Oct) is trailing. The PEG uses net-income growth NTM over TTM, not EPS growth, so buybacks are not in it; it is priced only inside the 10–100% growth band with three peers.
  • Forward P/E is market cap ÷ NTM net income, which bypasses ADR ratios and FMP share counts. Where FMP's consensus does not fit its own statements (NTM revenue outside 0.4–2.5× TTM) the consensus is dropped and the name goes in on trailing, marked T (Embraer was dropped from Boeing's set for this and Howmet took its place). Samsung's 2.7× consensus P/E is a data break caught by the under-4× rule and struck; its sales multiple stands.
  • Honeywell's trailing statements still carry the aerospace arm spun off on 29 Jun 2026, so its NTM-over-TTM growth and trailing margins are not like-for-like; the NTM rows (the remaining company) carry the read. Chevron's trailing year carries Hess from July 2025.
  • The steadiness block uses the dispersion of the Street's NTM EPS (high − low over mean) because FMP carries no estimate-revision history through the proxy; it is a proxy for revision risk, not a record of revisions. Revenue volatility is five year-on-year growth rates from six fiscal years; a company that made a large acquisition in the window (Chevron-Hess, Amgen-Horizon, Cisco-Splunk, Boeing-Spirit) is penalised by it, as it should be for this purpose.
  • Analysts' low · median · high are FMP's price-target consensus across all targets on file; the count shown is the last quarter's. The Hub's own checked-target table was not re-read.
  • No live Hub page was driven; nothing was deployed; no table was written; no key is printed in any file. No subagent and no paid model API were used.
PAGE SPECS · the rules, the sources, the FX, the tools

Rules

CW4 · from the raw FMP answers to every figure on the page. Deterministic: same raw, same JSON. The CW3 rules, plus
one rule for balance-sheet businesses and the steadiness block.

usage: python3 compute.py <peers.json> <deliverable dir> [today YYYY-MM-DD]

Rules (also printed on the page):
- ONE forward basis: next twelve months (NTM) = time-weighted blend of the two fiscal-year consensus rows that
straddle the next 12 months (FMP analyst-estimates, annual). w = days left in FY1 / 365.25. NTM = w·FY1 + (1−w)·FY2.
FY2 missing → FY1 alone, marked. No row → "no estimate"; a peer with no estimate goes in on trailing twelve
months (TTM) with a T mark.
- Price and market cap: FMP quote on the fetch date. EV = market cap + total debt (incl. leases, FMP's totalDebt)
− cash and short-term investments, latest quarterly balance sheet. All stated in USD at the fetch date's FX.
- Forward P/E = market cap ÷ NTM net income (so ADR ratios and share-count mismatches cannot bend it).
PEG = forward P/E ÷ NTM net-income growth in % (growth = NTM ÷ TTM − 1; needs both > 0). EV/sales and EV/EBITDA
on NTM. Gross margin TTM (consensus carries no gross profit). EBIT margin NTM (consensus EBIT ÷ consensus revenue).
Net debt ÷ TTM EBITDA.
- Balance-sheet businesses (banks, brokers, insurers, card lenders: GS, JPM, AXP, TRV and their bank and insurer
peers): EV, EV/sales, EV/EBITDA and net debt/EBITDA mean nothing and are not shown; they are priced on forward
P/E, PEG and price/book (market cap ÷ latest total shareholders' equity), with return on equity (TTM net income ÷
equity) and NTM net margin beside them; their revenue growth is consensus FY2 over FY1 (a bank's statement revenue
is gross of interest expense, consensus is net, so NTM over TTM would not compare). Card networks and processors
(V, MA, PayPal, Fiserv) are ordinary companies.
- Loss-maker: TTM net income ≤ 0 or NTM net income ≤ 0 (or no estimate). Priced on EV/sales (NTM) and EV/gross profit
(TTM); EV/EBITDA kept only when NTM EBITDA > 0.
- "Not meaningful": P/E over 100× or under 4×, EV/sales or EV/EBITDA over 60×, EV/EBITDA under 3×, PEG over 10, EV/gross
profit over 150×, P/B over 30× are printed struck and left out of the median; a row needs three meaningful peers to price. PEG is priced only
where NTM net-income growth is 10–100% with three peers carrying one.
- Implied price per multiple = peer median × the name's own figure, net debt taken out for EV rows, divided by shares
(market cap ÷ price). Midpoint = geometric middle of the lowest and highest implied price. Read: cheap when the
price is more than 15% under the midpoint; rich when more than 15% over; fair between.
- Mismatch: where FMP's consensus does not fit its own statements (NTM revenue outside 0.4–2.5× TTM) the consensus is a
unit or currency break (Embraer's was, on 20 Oct, so Howmet took its place); it is dropped and the name goes in on
trailing, marked T, with the reason printed. Net income is not tested this way: a trailing year depressed by a charge
(Merck's Verona write-off) makes a 6× recovery real, not a break; Samsung's 2.7× P/E is caught by the under-4× rule.
- Steadiness (the defensive block): NTM-EPS spread = (epsHigh − epsLow) ÷ epsAvg of the consensus rows, blended with
the same w (the dispersion of the Street's next-twelve-month EPS; FMP carries no revision history through the
proxy, so dispersion stands in for revision spread, and the page says so); 5-year revenue volatility = standard
deviation of the five year-on-year revenue growth rates from the last six fiscal-year income statements. The ten
steadiest = lowest sum of the two ranks across the 30.

  • FMP through the project's fmp-proxy edge function (stable routes: quote/batch-quote, profile, analyst-estimates annual, income-statement-ttm, balance-sheet-statement quarter, key-metrics-ttm; for the 30 also key-metrics-ttm, income-statement annual ×6, price-target-consensus, price-target-summary, grades-consensus, shares-float, cash-flow-statement quarter ×4, stock-peers). 1048 calls, 2026-10-20T16:31:44Z to 2026-10-20T16:38:42Z UTC, by status {"200": 1048}. Every answer is in COMPS-DOW30.json under raw.
  • The Dow list: lane's own list (FMP index-constituent route not on the proxy allow-list); constituents since 8 Nov 2024, taken 2026-10-20; GOOGL in for VZ before the open 29 Jun 2026; HON stays after the HONA spin (S&P DJI announcement 23 Jun 2026).
  • Foreign listings and their trading currency: 005930.KS (Samsung Electronics, KRW), 1810.HK (Xiaomi, HKD), AIR.PA (Airbus, EUR), 6301.T (Komatsu, JPY), SIE.DE (Siemens, EUR), NESN.SW (Nestle, CHF), ADS.DE (adidas, EUR), PUM.DE (Puma, EUR), AKZA.AS (AkzoNobel, EUR), 4612.T (Nippon Paint, JPY), ADYEN.AS (Adyen, EUR).
